bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 88 in `ot::Message::Write`. The staged 41-byte `radio-receive-done-fuzzer` witness is copied unchanged into `otRadioFrame.mPsdu`, then the OpenThread receive path admits it as an MLE Parent Request and dispatches to `ot::Mle::MleRouter::HandleParentRequest`. There, `Tlv::GetTlv(aMessage, Tlv::kChallenge, sizeof(challenge), challenge)` copies only 10 bytes into stack local `ChallengeTlv challenge` (the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte challenge field) but preserves the advertised Challenge length 88 in the copied header. `challenge.IsValid()` still accepts that object because `ChallengeTlv::IsValid()` only requires a length of at least 4. `SendParentResponse` then calls `AppendResponse(*message, aChallenge.GetChallenge(), aChallenge.GetLength())`, so the response builder reuses the attacker-controlled TLV header length instead of the clamped 8-byte challenge length. `AppendResponse` forwards that pointer-size pair into `Message::Append`, and `Message::Write` finally executes `memcpy(..., aBuf, bytesToCopy)` with `bytesToCopy = 88` while `aBuf` still points at the 8-byte challenge array inside stack local `challenge`. ASan reports the resulting stack overread at `message.cpp:595` and identifies `challenge` in `HandleParentRequest` as the overrun stack object. The fixing commit replaces the vulnerable `aChallenge.GetLength()` call with `aChallenge.GetChallengeLength()`, which caps the copy size at `sizeof(mChallenge) == 8`.

source.description: First project-side parse on the crashing path that materializes the attacker-controlled Challenge TLV into the fixed stack object later overread during response construction.
source.value_from: The staged 41-byte `poc` is passed unchanged to `otPlatRadioReceiveDone()`. On the reproduced path it is decoded as an MLE Parent Request whose Challenge TLV advertises length 88. This call copies that TLV into stack local `challenge` with `aMaxLength = sizeof(challenge) == 10`, preserving the header length 88 while only storing the first 8 challenge bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parse preserves the attacker-controlled Challenge length inside `challenge` and stores the fixed-size challenge bytes later referenced by `aChallenge.GetChallenge()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Because `sizeof(challenge) == 10`, the copied stack object contains only the 2-byte TLV header plus the 8-byte `mChallenge` array even though the saved ASan trace shows the stored header length later drives an 88-byte read.

sink.description: ASan sink. `Message::Write` copies `bytesToCopy` bytes from the forwarded Challenge pointer without checking that the source still fits in the fixed 8-byte challenge field.
sink.note: On the crashing path `aBuf` still aliases the challenge bytes inside stack local `challenge` from `HandleParentRequest`, and `bytesToCopy` becomes 88. ASan reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 88` here and identifies `challenge` at `mle_router.cpp:1563` as the overrun stack object.

root_cause.description: The response builder reuses the incoming TLV header length as the outbound copy size instead of the fixed/clamped Challenge field length.
root_cause.note: `ChallengeTlv::GetChallengeLength()` already clamps to `sizeof(mChallenge)`, and the fixing commit changes this call site to use that accessor. Reusing `aChallenge.GetLength()` here is the missing size obligation that makes the later `memcpy()` read past stack local `challenge`.

parser_admitted.description: The MLE header has already been decoded and classified as a Parent Request, so the receive path dispatches into the router-side Parent Request parser instead of rejecting the packet.

fine_trace.note: The MLE parser finds the request's Challenge TLV and copies it into stack local `challenge`. On the witnessed path `ot::Tlv::Get()` first reads a Challenge header whose length is 88, then re-reads only `sizeof(challenge) == 10` bytes total, so the copied object keeps header length 88 but contains only the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte `mChallenge` field.

The validity gate accepts the oversized object because `ChallengeTlv::IsValid()` only requires `GetLength() >= kMinSize` (4) and does not enforce `<= kMaxSize` (8). With stored length 88, execution stays on the response path instead of rejecting the malformed TLV.

Root cause. This call forwards the fixed Challenge field pointer together with the attacker-controlled TLV header length, so the outbound response size becomes 88 instead of the clamped Challenge length 8. The patch replaces `aChallenge.GetLength()` with `aChallenge.GetChallengeLength()`.

The response builder records the same 88-byte length in the outgoing Response TLV header and asks `Message::Append` to copy 88 bytes from `aResponse`. `aResponse` still aliases the 8-byte challenge array stored in step 1's stack object.

Sink. `Message::Append` forwards `aResponse` and `aResponseLength` into `Write`, and on the first copy iteration `bytesToCopy` becomes 88. `aBuf` still points at the 8-byte `mChallenge` field inside stack local `challenge`, so this `memcpy()` reads 88 bytes from a 10-byte stack object and overruns its end. The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 88` here and names `challenge` at `mle_router.cpp:1563` as the overflowed object.

format.name: OpenThread radio-receive-done raw radio frame
format.contract: Exactly the staged 41-byte witness `41 20 20 7f 3b 02 f2 20 4d 4c 20 ff 00 15 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 09 03 ff 00 00 12 02 20 20 0e 01 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20`. The harness copies these bytes unchanged into `otRadioFrame.mPsdu`, sets `frame.mLength = 41` and `frame.mChannel = 11`, and calls `otPlatRadioReceiveDone()`. On the witnessed path the frame reaches `HandleParentRequest()` with a parsed Challenge TLV whose stored header length is 88, so `SendParentResponse()` later copies 88 bytes from the fixed 8-byte challenge field. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger class beyond this exact witness.
